turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll research the openai-node repository structure using the gh CLI to locate streaming implementation.Good, found the key files. Let me examine the core streaming implementation and how it's wired to public API methods.Now let's find where `Stream` is instantiated — i.e., which API resource methods create a stream (base client + resource files).I now have a complete picture. Let me verify the base `APIResource`/client `_client.post` call path connects to `defaultParseResponse` (already confirmed via `parse.ts`), and check the ResponseStream and ChatCompletionStream `createX` static methods briefly for completeness.I have enough evidence now to answer comprehensively.

## Where streaming is implemented

**Core SSE engine:** `src/core/streaming.ts` (re-exported for backward compat by the deprecated `src/streaming.ts`)
- `Stream<Item>` class — implements `AsyncIterable<Item>`. Two constructors:
  - `Stream.fromSSEResponse(response, controller, client?, synthesizeEventData?)` — parses a `fetch` `Response` as Server-Sent Events (via the internal `_iterSSEMessages`/`SSEDecoder`/`LineDecoder`), yielding parsed JSON chunks, stopping at `data: [DONE]`, and surfacing `{error}` payloads as `APIError`.
  - `Stream.fromReadableStream(readableStream, controller, client?)` — parses a newline-delimited JSON `ReadableStream` (used to rehydrate a stream that was serialized with `.toReadableStream()`, e.g. for Vercel Edge/Next.js proxying).
  - Also provides `.tee()` (fork into two independently-consumable streams) and `.toReadableStream()`.

**Where a request becomes a `Stream`:** `src/internal/parse.ts` → `defaultParseResponse()`. When `FinalRequestOptions.stream` is truthy, instead of `response.json()` it calls `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)` (or a custom `props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(...)` if the resource method set one, e.g. for image partial-JSON events). This is the single choke point all streaming responses pass through — the resource methods just set `stream: true/false` on the request options; `defaultParseResponse` decides the return type.

**Higher-level ergonomic wrappers** (built on top of `Stream`), all under `src/lib/`:
- `src/lib/EventStream.ts` — abstract base class (`EventStream<Events>`) providing `.on()`/`.emit()`, `.done()`, `.abort()`, async-iteration plumbing, used by the two concrete stream helpers below.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` — `ChatCompletionStream` (extends `AbstractChatCompletionRunner`, itself presumably built on `EventStream`-like machinery), assembles incremental `ChatCompletionChunk`s into a running `ChatCompletion` snapshot and emits semantic events (`content`, `chunk`, `message`, etc.). Static entry point `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion(client, params, options)`.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` — streaming variant of the tool-calling runner (`runTools`).
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` — `ResponseStream` (extends `EventStream<ResponseEvents>`), same idea for the Responses API (`ResponseStreamEvent`s → snapshot). Static entry point `ResponseStream.createResponse(client, params, options)`.
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — `AssistantStream` (extends `EventStream<AssistantStreamEvents>`) for the (deprecated) Assistants/Threads/Runs API. Static entries: `createAssistantStream`, `createThreadAssistantStream`, `createToolAssistantStream`, plus `fromReadableStream`.

## Public API methods that route into it

All of these set `stream: body.stream ?? false` (or similar) on the request passed to `this._client.post/get(...)`, which flows through `defaultParseResponse` into `Stream.fromSSEResponse`:

| Method | File | Return when `stream:true` |
|---|---|---|
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:70-79` | `Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(params)` | same file, `:221-226` | `ChatCompletionStream` (helper) |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools({stream:true})` | same file, `:200-216` | `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner` |
| `client.completions.create({stream:true})` (legacy) | `src/resources/completions.ts:29-43` | `Stream<Completion>` |
| `client.responses.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-123` | `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve(id, {stream:true})` | same file, `:140-169` | `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.stream(params)` | same file, `:201-206` | `ResponseStream` (helper) |
| `client.images.edit({stream:true})` | `src/resources/images.ts:46-61` | `Stream<ImageEditStreamEvent>` |
| `client.images.generate({stream:true})` | same file, `:79-93` | `Stream<ImageGenStreamEvent>` |
| `client.audio.transcriptions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts:47-...` | `Stream<TranscriptionStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create(threadId, {stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:62-82` | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(threadId, body)` | same file, `:232` | `AssistantStream` (helper) |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputs(..., {stream:true})` | same file, `:253-273` | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputsStream(...)` | same file, `:296-302` | `AssistantStream` (helper) |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRun({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts:147-163` | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |

Not verified: I read only the resource/lib files above, not `src/client.ts`'s full request-building path (confirmed it does *not* itself branch on `stream`), nor the `AbstractChatCompletionRunner`/`AbstractAssistantStreamRunner` base classes' internals, nor `src/resources/audio/speech.ts`'s `sse` stream_format handling (it appears to return raw octet-stream/binary rather than going through `Stream`, based on the `Accept: application/octet-stream` header seen, but I didn't trace that fully). I also did not check `src/resources/beta/realtime` / `src/resources/realtime` (WebSocket-based, a separate transport from the SSE `Stream` class) beyond noting their existence.
